children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures managed to forgo earlier losses to finish with small increases. The sharp turnaround in crude-oil prices led to the about-face.
European rapeseed also posted slight gains, while Malaysian palm oil was mixed. Losses in the Chicago soy complex closed softer.

An analyst said Wednesday that producer deliveries of canola have been picking up because of the improved weather on the Prairies, as well as more harvest progress. The analyst added that with the trade having a better idea of the size of Canada's canola crop, its risk premium has been largely removed.

The analyst also said China purchased canola from Australia for the first time since 2020. He suggested that could lead to China buying more of the oilseed from Australia at the expense of its imports from Canada.

Over the next couple of days, Prairie temperatures are to range from the high teens to the mid 20s Celsius. Rain is expected for much of southern Manitoba, while the rest of the Prairies are to remain dry.
Manitoba Agriculture reported the province's canola harvest reached 43% complete. The crop's quality was said to be below average to average.
Saskatchewan is set to issue its crop report on Thursday.
The Canadian dollar was stepping back at 70.93 U.S. cents, compared to Tuesday's close of 71.10.
There were 59,825 canola contracts traded on Wednesday, compared to 54,956 on Tuesday. Spreading accounted for 31,290 contracts traded.
